tips.comment: No comment made
Poor start last time out scuppered his chances. Kept on when winning in his penultimate race over 6 furlongs and was squeezed for room over his last 7 furlong run.
A 7 time course and distance winner is a hard record to ignore. Nearest the finish when going third of eleven over a mile here last time out and should go well again dropping back to 7 furlongs.

Jkr Cobbler is a three-time Ayr winner and has winning form over today's 7f trip on this track. He resumed in decent style to finish second on 7 July over this course and distance, just beaten by three-quarters of a length. Following that run, he has been given almost three weeks off, a break that may rejuvenate him for today's effort. Rated just OR64, he looks well treated off that mark, especially over this C&D. A strongly paced race should play into his hands, given his closing style.

Dual 7f winner last autumn and shaped with promise in April/May, but not built on that since. Traffic issues encountered when eased and beaten 5 1/2l here last time, so that run was better than it suggests. Draw to overcome but chancing it today.

After showing very little, Jammas Journey has suddenly blossomed into a winning machine. She won at Hamilton less than a fortnight ago and then followed up here last Monday. She won both races well, but she absolutely hacked up last week, and the penalty is unlikely to stop her running up the hat-trick.
Went third close to home over a furlong further at Musselburgh on the 1st of July, remains on the same mark and should welcome this drop in trip.

Made debut in a hot race that has been well advertised by the front two home that day who have won a Group 2, a Group 3 and a Listed race between them. Bred to be decent and the two siblings out of dam to hit the track have both been good sorts including the filly Pink Crystal who ended up a C&D Winner here as a 4yo here. Might need more time but should improve for debut and yard did have a 2yo winner yesterday. Lots to like and can run well.

Consistent runner but hasn't got his head in front for a year. Cheekpieces reapplied for the first time since 2023. Worth noting that the first time cheekpieces were applied in 2023, he did win, so worth thinking they can eke out that bit of extra.
No comment made
4-year-old goes well at Ayr. 4/12 here last time out a week ago. Regular jockey for the Goldie yard on board. Could go well given a liking for the track.

A 7-race maiden and unplaced in all those races urges caution, but she was only beaten by a length and a half over a furlong further here 2 weeks ago. The drop in trip and a falling mark of 55 could help her break that maiden tag.

Crown Of Oaks has finished 3rd in all three of his starts so far. He steps up in trip for his handicap debut, and with William Haggis having an excellent record here at Ayr, he looks the most likely winner on handicap debut.

Hasn't troubled the judge in 3yo career yet but has run well in some competitive races. One I've followed as though has stamina to prove I thought would easily get 10f as dam had won herself as a 3yo at 1m2f and 1m3.5f. Won here on debut before coming back here to be beaten a neck in second start so obviously handles the track and could well take some beating in this. Has run well in class 2 and 3 races and was arguably unlucky dropping into this grade last time as was hampered at a crucial time. Big chance if definitely seeing out the trip and I can't see why he won't and emulate his dam as a 3yo.

I may be completely wrong, but I cannot for the life of me see why Crown Of Oaks is as short a price favourite as he is. I know he comes from the stable of William Haggas, but there is nothing in his form that suggests he can take this handicap. If anything, I think he may be regressive rather than progressive. The next two in the betting are far more appealing. Austrian Theory had some good form in some strong handicaps when trained by Charlie Johnston, and Tim Easterby has one win with him under his belt, with more to come I expect. He was an excellent fifth in the John Smith's Cup at York last time, and has actually been dropped a pound for that. This is a much easier opportunity than that ultra-competitive handicap, and he must have every chance of winning.
Sir Mark Prescott brings this former course and distance winner a long way for this race and the drop in trip and first time blinkers could make this a worthwhile journey.

This 4-year-old Irish filly has surged forward in progression in recent weeks, winning over 1m 4f at Haydock earlier this month and running a close third over the same trip on a previous outing. She displayed strong stamina and consistency. Her recent win was on good turf, so it should suit today. Trainer Lucinda Russell is in great form, and jockey Oisin Orr continues to get the best from her.

Top jockey back on. This horse did incredibly well last race. It was ridden by a 5-pound claimer. The jockey didn't even whip the horse once from 2 furlongs out. The horse did make up a lot of ground in soft conditions. Today's extra furlong is going to help with the good jockey booking.

I do think every now and again horses you can class as veterans are written off too readily, especially if there's still some fairly recent form in the locker. GLASSES UP fits the bill here with that course hat-trick recorded here as recently as May. Poor since then but only a pound above last winning mark and difficult to rule out, even with some potential young improvers in this field.
Zuffolo made a hash of the start at Catterick last time, yet managed to run on to finish third. Assuming he breaks better this time he can win this very average handicap.
He has won from this mark before and did show some promise staying on at the end of his last race. Improvement is needed but not that much, so he can get involved this afternoon.
Showed a lot of promise earlier in the season. Horse is great each way value in this field. Should go close at a huge price.
Ran lazily when slowly away last race but finished very well. If the claimer can get a better position, stands every chance. Dropped a couple of pounds also. RPRs look good and likes it around here.
No comment made

Dwindling Funds is a Jim Goldie horse that has been given a very odd campaign thus far. He only started racing this season at four years of age. Initially, he was tried around a mile. That wasn't successful, so he was tried over sprint trips. Unsurprisingly, that proved fruitless, so the last two tries have been at a mile and a half or further. Whilst that was only marginally better than what went before, he did, at least, look as though there might be a little ability there. Now he tries a mile and a quarter in a very poor race. It's anyone's guess if this will be his trip, but at a double-figure price, I'm prepared to have a small each-way play.

As with many of Sir Mark Prescott's horses, String Of Pearls has improved for stepping up in trip in handicaps. Unplaced in 3 runs last year, she was 5th at Newmarket on her handicap debut and then won a 5-runner handicap at Goodwood over 1m4f last month. The step up to 1m6f should see more improvement, and up just 4lbs, she has a good chance of following up.

Kotari is a 6-year-old mare trained by Gary & Josh Moore. She hasn't been in the best of form in 2025 but landed a hat-trick of wins in 2024, winning off marks of 73-77-82, the latter in a class 3 handicap at Ascot. Today's soft ground won't present any problems as she won on heavy ground at Salisbury off 77, so she won't mind any more rain. She's been running in better-graded races than today's fair and runs off a lowly 65 with Ashley Lewis's 7lb claim. Given she posted a near career-high RPR of 91 at Ascot, she could be literally chucked in at the weights if the yard has her fitness anywhere near what it's been in some of her back form.
On a winning streak and no reason not to pursue. Distance suits as won twice as favorite. Was competitive over a longer distance when placed.
Switches back to flats after a couple of runs over jumps. Did win last performance on the flat at Southwell last month, which was off a higher mark. A drop down in class should help.

With a career record of 1 win and 4 places from 10 starts, George has shown steady improvement, especially on turf. His recent form figures, 2nd, 3rd, 2nd, 1st, suggest a horse hitting his stride. Back at Yarmouth for the Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs, he returns to the same track and distance where he scored last time, now rated 56.

Ataser is a 7-year-old gelding trained by T G Kent. He is a four-time winner, winning three times over today's trip off marks of 79, 86, and 82, all coming in class 2 on good ground contests. So, clearly well handicapped due to a series of poor efforts. He runs today in a class 6 for the first time, which obviously is company in which Ataser would eat for breakfast in his prime. Not quite the force of old, but in this company off a mark of 63, he has to enter calculations. Another reason is T G Kent's current form in handicaps. He is 33/183 wins and 74/283 placed since 2023, showing a healthy LSP of £60.87 and £40.63 each way. T J Kent also has success at Yarmouth with 6/25 wins in handicaps, showing a LSP of £19.33. If 10-1 or less in handicaps this significantly increas, his last eight runners have finished 1-2-1-4-1-2-1-1, winning with Dream Pirate 4-1, Mister Mojito (twice 10-30, 6-1), Zenzic 10-1, and Drifts Away 6-1. A welterweight of 10st and the soft ground are negatives, but Ataser will slam this lot if Kent has him anywhere near peak fitness.

The owners of this unexposed 3yo have some really decent runners with this trainer, and I'd be highly surprised if a mark of just 65 didn't underestimate her ability. The trainer has booked a jockey who does well for him too and who rides this course particularly well. The half-length 2nd at Thirsk was when between horses rated around 10lb more than her mark here, and the trainer's runners are going well at the moment, so the 18/1 looks well worth taking.

Spent some time looking at this one. It comes down to 4 horses, and with odds on offer, it's too hard to turn these down. Spencer has some okay horses and is running well. This has some decent siblings who handle the ground. Last run can be ignored, and I can see this one running well over its mark, thrown in with the allowance. Let's see.

Monastry is a 2-year-old colt trained by T J Kent. He made a promising debut at Haydock, beaten just 1.75 lengths, and did well in the circumstances: 'Held up in rear, headway on outer 2f out, kept on final 110 yards' under today's jockey Adam Farragher. The 1/10 Amakhala Warrior, the 5/10 Renovatio Angel, 7/10 Snake Charmer, and Penhallam, also 7/10, all won on their next starts at 5-4, 16-1, 9-4, and 14-1 respectively, so a hot maiden. Monastry, out of a once-raced dam called Vital Force (78) trained by John Gosden and bred by Godolphin, can take a step forward today with experience now under his belt.

This looks like a solid each-way bet with a fair chance of winning. Was unlucky last time, well-bred, and the ground shouldn't be an issue. Has a few lbs to claw back vs. the favorite, but hoping for the second-time bounce.

The jockey rides this track very well. Yes, this is a big price, but we are about to see the best of this horse very soon. I think today is the day. Ground trip will suit, going by breeding. Big shout today.

Hinitsa Bay won his first ever race over course and distance last time out after finishing 2nd twice earlier this year. He is up four pounds but still on a lowly mark of 52 and he was off the track for 618 days so did not run as a three year old. He could improve further for Ian Williams.

Duffus Castle is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Phillip McBride and owned by C Massie & PJ McBride. It is ridden by Harry Davies. (4/7) wins for C Massie & PJ McBride on the Phillip McBride-trained Priscilla's Wish, and it won 7 times at Yarmouth. Harry Davies rode him to victory four times. Duffus Castle remains a maiden after 7 starts and opened on a handicap mark of 62. It runs today off a career-low mark of 47, having been run over a variety of trips. Phillip McBride trains down the road at Newmarket and has picked up 48/293 wins at Yarmouth, showing a LSP of £97.33. Duffus Castle is out of a dam trained by Phillip McBride, who won two races off 52-59, which incidentally both came at today's track, Yarmouth, adding an intriguing backstory.

A single victory from 32 flat races was at this venue. He came in 10th, in a handicap at this course and distance 19 days ago. Nevertheless, I don't think this 5-year-old is out of the race yet. Brandon Wilkie will be riding this time and has been performing well. His 3lb claim could be advantageous, and at 40/1 an each-way bet could provide a substantial return.
Typeface has not been great in his three runs so far, but that means he does come into this handicap debut on a decent mark and drops to C6 EW 4P.

After missing by just a neck, Rolling Luck returns with unfinished business. This lightly raced 3-year old has found his groove over longer trips, and today's conditions mirror the setup of his standout performance. His pedigree screams stamina, perfect for grinding out a win over 10+ furlongs.
Soft ground would be a worry, but he drops into a lowly classified stakes race here and was unlucky over course and distance on penultimate start. Worth taking a chance.
NAP of the day, which I've gone each way just in case. I think this should be the favorite, well related to soft ground siblings. CD winner last run, same jockey, all systems go.

Fen Tiger is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Julia & Shelley Birkett. He is a three-time winner in class 6 handicaps on good to soft, soft, and heavy over 1m 4f, so conditions suit. Fen Tiger showed signs of a revival on his last start over CD behind four of today's rivals, beaten 3.75 lengths under Frederick Larson (no claim) : 'In rear, headway from over 2f out, outpaced over 1f out, stayed on inside final furlong.' But that was on good ground, and with more optimal conditions presenting themselves today, Fen Tiger can finish strongly late on in proceedings in more 
favorable mucky ground, having won thrice over 1m 4f, a 1/2f further than today's trip. Yet to win at Yarmouth, but he has fared well in the last three attempts at the track: 2(0.75l); 2(1.5l) and 5(3.75l) and today connections put up a 7lb apprentice today in the shape of Chloe Lyons which should help reverse recent form with her rivals. Julia & Shelley Birkett train locally at Newmarket and are 5/16 wins at Yarmouth showing a healthy LSP of £24.25 and the 14-1 looks a tad overpriced.
Bond Spirit has not had much luck of late after not getting a clear run for the last two outings, but is 4 lbs below his last turf winning mark from last year and worth an EW chance.
Naughty Niall was denied on the nod last time out at Yarmouth and despite a rise of a pound for that run, can go one better here with De Soussa booked for the first time.

No wins in 8 starts, but has run some eye-catching races in defeat. Closing from the back of the pack last time for 2nd is a positive form line. Runs better with a bit of cut in the ground and can go well again.

Backing Twilight Guest, the 5-year-old Twilight Son gelding trained by G. G. Margarson, in tomorrow’s Play At The Races StableDuel Handicap over 1m 2f 23y at Yarmouth. He heads into action off the back of a consistent run of form this season??'three wins and a second from just eight starts??'with his latest outing at Brighton seeing him finish fourth of five, beaten 3¾ lengths in a Class 6 handicap over this trip .
Rated 60, he brings value for money into this competitive field. Notably, he scored at Pontefract earlier this summer and that run showed his ability to handle consistent front-of-pack race patterns . Set to be ridden by D. Egan, who handles his hold-up style well, it’s expected he’ll be settled mid-pack before being delivered into the race in the closing stages on Yarmouth’s galloping track.
In a 10-runner Class 6 handicap, and seen around 4/1 (11/2) in the market, Twilight Guest offers solid each-way appeal given his proven seasonal consistency, ideal distance profile, and well-handled race style.

Small each-way bet on this, which looks like a tight little race. The four I fancied to outrun their odds are the top three in the market, then the selection. So, at the odds, it's worth a small bet. Well related and falling down the weights and a change of scenery.

Tilsworth Silver is a 4-year-old gelding trained by John Jenkins and owned by M Ng. He is 0-10 and has shown absolutely nothing of note. Out of an unraced dam and related to 3 winners (all won on good to soft or soft (2)), two were trained byJenkins and owned by M Ng, sprinters: Tilsworth Only Ta (5) and Tilsworth Rose (4). So why is Jenkins suddenly stepping Tilsworth Silver up in trip to 1m 2f today, a trip never run over before (7f being the furthest) on soft ground not ever encountered. But there may be an angle, as the dam was a half- sister to three others who all won, two of which performed best over 12f +. The selection is also a half-sister to Monaco Rose, who won four times over 12f, so there may be some hope. Oliver Carmichael rides, and he claims 7lb to run off 39 some 2lb below her official mark of 41. He's picked up four winners for Eve Johnson Houghton at 6-1, 17-2, 25-1, and 28-1 so not afraid to pop one in at a big price. Whilst this is a speculative selection at 80-1, we have nothing to lose.

This 3-year-old filly was beaten 2 1/4 lengths in second behind the well-backed A M Balding-trained Fantasy World over one mile two furlongs on good to soft ground at Ffos Las on her racecourse debut 28 days ago. With the stable of trainer W J Haggas in such good form, she can go one place better today.

Short price favorite, but for good reason. From a powerful yard, it ran a really good race on debut, beaten by a Cox horse with the third winning and running to a 90. This should be straightforward with some low standard opposition.

Hello Youmzain colt who was last seen at York where finishing 9th/11 however he veered sharply too the left coming out the gates and lost many lenghts at the start as a result however despite that he showed he was a horse with plenty of potential and the manor he closed up with after losing many lenghts at the start was pretty good in my point of view in top hands back home and if breaking on terms as expected this time out W J Haggas's inmate is likely to be a whole different proposition this time out and is most certainly no horse to underestimate here jockey Tom Marquand takes the ride and can give Art Lover a promising ride here at Windsor considered
Better than ever in his last 2 runs and is back down in class/grade here. Connections put up a 5lb claimer, so on these terms, he should really be winning this.

The stable is ticking over, and they have upped their standards of races. They are trying to win better races, so I'm going with Calibos tonight. They have a good jockey onboard tonight, and the trip and ground are fine, so a big race is expected.
Makes debut for Ross Burdon and has shown some decent form in the past, perhaps over longer trips than today. We'll take a chance the change of scenery may bring about some improvement.
Waiting for room 2 furlongs out but ceded first run to the winner, but 2nd of 18. Remains on the same mark and every chance to go one better on these terms.
Down in grade, Billy up on board, I fancy this to run a good race here. Put up a good time LTO, expecting this one to burn its rivals off here in an open race. Win only.

Many a Star is a great horse that Jamie has great faith in. He can win this race, giving him a double in the last two races. Trip and ground are okay, so I can't see this horse not being in the frame.

Despite being relatively unexposed, Big Cyril looks poised for improvement stepping up to this Class 3 6f sprint handicap on good to firm ground. Trained by Alice Hynes, he carries just 9-9 in weights. His recent runs fall short of what he's capable of, which explains his price today, but the addition of first-time cheekpieces should sharpen him up. I have to give him a second look at this price.

Excuses the last twice, having met trouble in running on penultimate start before having his saddle slip last time. Now down a couple of pounds here and dropped significantly in grade. Decent chance here.

Top Biller isn't bulletproof, but he's knocking on the door. I think tonight can be the night. Well drawn and ran well here last time out at a shorter trip. Being stepped back up to 6f should suit perfectly. A return visit from connections is usually a positive to take from it also. Sean Levey's only ride for the day. If the race gets hot early doors and we get the timing right, I can see us being the one to beat.

Backing All Too Beautiful, the lightly raced 3-year-old filly by Bated Breath, in today’s 6f Class 6 handicap.
Although she’s still seeking a breakthrough win, her latest outing at Leicester saw her run with real credit??'finishing a solid third of seven, sticking on well and only beaten 3½ lengths by Currahee off a mark of 52, showing there’s definite potential to improve from that effort . Her previous form includes mixed results, but that Leicester run appears to be a step in the right direction under Mason Paetel for trainer R A Teal .
While she isn’t the standout on paper, she’s unexposed (only six starts) and handles good to good??'to??'firm ground well. In a small field of 12 runners and with Paetel’s 5??'lb apprentice claim, she carries plenty of each-way appeal at likely odds around 10/1??'12/1??'especially if the pace unfolds playfully up front .
Piranha Rama, a 3-year-old bay filly, dropped 3 pounds for her last run over a trip too short. Back over 6 furlongs for this run, she could be more competitive here. Each way price.
With Billy on board and up in triple, Love Rock can go well here. Unexposed on the turf and looks like there is a bit of potential.
Golden Thorn, for me, is one to keep on side. Still, first-time blinkers should have a really positive effect for this one to progress. The one to beat.

Final Bet ran a good race the time before last after a slow start, beating a horse who has gone on to better things since. Held up last LTO in a quick race and never quite got into it. A much weaker race here, and I can see this going close.
Midsummer Music is from a shrewd yard, and Tom is on tonight. So, a big run is expected, and I'm on tonight. Let's pray we win and get the bookies before the Goodwood week.

This Dr. R Newland & J Insole trained colt won on his racecourse debut over six furlongs at Wolverhampton 35 days ago when keeping on well to easily beat the I Furtado trained Alfa Duplicate by 4 1/4 lengths. So, with improvement likely, he looks hard to beat with Hollie Doyle back in the plate.

Won off this mark on the all weather at Kempton in March 2025 and drops in trip after racing over a mile there last time out. Represents the in-form Ed Dunlop yard who have 5 winners from their last 16 runners.

A 6 times career winner who won 4 times last year including over this CD last August. Not disgraced in all 3 starts so far this year and is now 4lbs below the last winning mark so a good run is expected.

Silver Trumpet really likes the AW and Southwell, winning over this course and distance in the past. His trainer, Eve Houghten, is in fine form and looks like he's made good progression since his wind operation. I think he should go close today, and the price offered for him in the double digits is generous.

Backing Ultramarine, the 6-year-old Zoffany gelding trained by P. D. Evans and ridden by Fred Daly, in tomorrow’s Join Southwell Golf Club Handicap (Class 4, 7f 14y). This one steps back onto Tapeta, where he’s a five-time winner and clearly at home.
Recent efforts include a victory on AW at Chepstow in June, followed by a slightly disappointing run when sixth of 13 at Chester a few weeks later??'but that may reflect stamina stretch or firmer going than his ideal surface . Before that, his form reads 653116: two wins sandwiched around solid Class 4 performances??'showing he handles this grade when conditions suit .
Carrying a mark of 82, he steps into this 13-runner field under a well-judged 7 lb claim from Fred Daly, who has ridden him before. Expect him to be delivered from rear mid-field, building into the race on Southwell’s long straight. His AW proficiency, recent win, and rising fitness give him a strong each-way case.

MASTER RICHARD returns to the all-weather from a significantly reduced mark, so he might be able to turn the tide on a disappointing turf campaign here. His last three runs in this grade and on this surface were fourth-placed finishes from much higher in the handicap, so maybe this switch is what the doctor ordered.

Has been struggling for a couple of years to be competitive but poses much more of a threat on AW. So should welcome the switch back to this surface and hoping 11 lbs lighter than last winning mark makes the difference.

Lord Abama ran another solid race at Haydock last time, and there's nothing to believe he won't do so again. He appears to have the best form overall and has won on an artificial surface a couple of times already. With the Michael Dods stable in good form, he looks the one.

My best bet for Monday (win bet, not each-way) and well supported already. Has taken well to sprinting and won narrowly at Pontefract over 6f. Not disgraced next time when fourth beaten 1 1/2 lengths when running over 5f. The return to 6f looks perfect and has a strong chance in a competitive sprint.

Will strip fitter on third start since joining Adrian Wintle last month having not seen a racecourse for 228 days prior to that. Eased in grade after racing in a Class 4 at Wolverhampton last time out and could go well at a decent price.

This C Appleby-trained colt must be going well at home, as he was a well-backed favourite for his racecourse debut over seven furlongs on good to firm ground at Sandown. He was beaten by 1 1/4 lengths in third behind his stablemate Pacifica Pier. With improvement expected and W Buick back in the saddle, he looks hard to oppose.

I never thought I would ever tip a Sir Mark Prescott 2-year-old debutant at 25/1 (most bookies), but this one cost 260k. It is beyond comprehension that the trainer would run this one down the field in 3 maidens to get a low handicap mark to win a class 6 race as a 3-year-old. The Godolphin horse is favorite but let connections down when beaten at odds-on on debut.
4/11 earlier this month at Haydock was a real stride forward in his form. Set off at 11/1. If he can build on that in what looks like a slightly easier race, then he has place claims.

Backing Eden Storm, the 5-year-old Starspangledbanner gelding trained by Patrick Morris, in tomorrow’s Highbet Weekly Racing Rewards Club ‘Confined’ Handicap (1m 13y, Class 6 Tapeta) at Southwell.
He returns dropping into this restricted Class 6 grade off a mark of 57, having been running in Class 4 company most recently. His latest effort came at Wolverhampton in May??'finishing a respectable 5th of 13 when looking hard fit and showing he stays the trip and handles Tapeta well . Prior to that, Eden Storm posted third-place finishes at AW before-only in similarly tough events, showing consistency over his 12 AW starts with a couple of wins in the book .
He also boasts a 33% course & distance strike rate, proving he knows how to handle Southwell’s demanding surface??'where stamina over worn ground is king . Trainer Morris has had a steady summer, and with Jack Nicholls again booked (he was aboard for that Wolverhampton run), expect a confident ride to settle Eden Storm mid-pack before winding up his challenge in the final furlong.

The use of cheekpieces for the first time did not have the desired effect LTO when only 11 of 12 at Ayr earlier this month. So, hoping switch to blinkers for the first time and drop down in class does the trick.

Magdalayna struggles over longer trips, but the trip here looks to suit her better. This will be her first run on an artificial surface, so she's unproven here. But on the flip side, she might actually suit it better. She's lightly raced and only carrying 9-8. There is room for progression, especially back at a mile. I'm expecting a bold run if she takes to the AW.
Dance Recital is a tricky one to follow, but I think the re-stepping back up to a mile should be the thing to make this horse click. 4 places on offer looks like a good each way play.

Aiden O'Brien usually targets this race for some reason, usually with a once-raced, less-exposed type. Here he relies on Constitution River, who ran really well in his only race at Newmarket behind a useful-looking Godolphin horse, and he should be good enough to win this.
Davy Crockett was an impressive nine length winner of his only bumper at Punchestown last month and probably only has the experienced hurdler Ephesus to beat here at Galway.

Plenty of promise on the flat as a 3-year-old last year before winning a maiden over 1m4f at Bellewstown on seasonal return back in April. Won a maiden hurdle over 2 miles at Punchestown on penultimate start, then finished a close second in a novice hurdle over 2m1f at Bellewstown 23 days ago, with the front two pulling well clear of the field. Good each-way chance on that form.

The model I run suggests Snow White Park can win this one. Snow White Park lines up here with the third highest RPR of this 12-runner field but has been well treated in the weights. Steps out carrying an equal weight to the majority of other runners and has Danny Mullins on board picking up the reins. Came first when last out 61 days ago and looks to go well again after a short break. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
There is a strong favorite in this race, but a nice each-way chance for this one with a top jockey booking noted.

Too Bossy For Us is very much the first string of the two Willie Mullins-trained horses here. Patrick Mullins rides (Grand National winning jockey). The selection is a four-year-old by Derby and Arc Winner Golden Horn. Ran second of 25 to a stablemate at a very similar staying trip to this at the Curragh recently. Beaten favourite that day, but it was a strong effort. Up a few pounds but still looks to hold a good chance in this company. Good horses down the years, but they look a bit jaded compared to this clearly progressive 4yo who ran very well on sole Flat start for this yard so far (won a Class 3 at Ascot when with Kevin Philippart De Foy). Worth backing at odds of 5-1.
Comfort Zone has crept up the handicap, but he is a decent stayer on the flat and over hurdles. J P O'Brien's horses are in form, and he was a close 3rd at Royal Ascot over two and a half miles.

Won at this meeting last year and remains unexposed at the trip after a good 2nd in the Naas Premier Handicap at the back end of last season. 3 lbs higher here but surely laid out for this and ran well over hurdles LTO as a solid prep. 9L 5th at Bellewstown, shaping like it would improve for the run.

Third in last year's Dante shows he has class and though moved from Owen Burrows yard to Ireland shouldn't put one off thinking this one could still make up into a good sort. Step up in trip looks sure to suit as has run two crackers at 1m6f just being denied each time and shaping as if 2m would suit. Has a half brother out of dam who has won a bumper and hurdle race over 2m so there is every chance this one could relish that trip now. Is thoroughly unexposed and though didn't trouble the judge last time at Royal Ascot plodded in in a good handicap over a trip that now looks too short. Huge chance for me in race where many look pretty exposed. Is mad to think was taking on the likes of Calandagan this time last year and could be a cut above these. EW banker for me is seeing it out and I can't see why he won't.

Plontier is another that is getting on a bit, but the last win in August was after a break. Although a bit duff since, the last two runs in December and January were in a G2 and a G1. It's worth an EW shot while back in handicap with 5P on offer.
Based purely on recent form MON COEUR would have no chance but he very much likes this course and his trainer has a good record at this meeting so a small each way wager might just pay dividends.

The model I run suggests a huge upset by Wahraan. This result has been driven by Wahraan having the second highest RPR of this huge 20 horse field. Mr. Healy on board relieves a further 7 lbs and tries the tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration. Huge odds on offer due to lack of form, but there is a huge weight differential here taking into account the initial weight difference and claiming jockey. That surely shows over the 2m trip and can go close if anywhere near back to form. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Placed in a flat handicap for Alan King. Twice placed in 3 year old hurdles. Latest 3rd reads well with the winner and 2nd now rated 118 and 127. Gets into this handicap off 105 and looks well handicapped.

Trainer Ross O'Sullivan has a good record at this meeting, and his 6yo looks to have been laid out for this, with a spin on the flat 27 days ago. He'll be strong at the finish, and this testing track will suit him down to the ground.

Tell Us This won a handicap hurdle over 2m1f at Down Royal in May of last year, followed by a good second at Ballinrobe after that, though not so good in the final 3 starts. Was impressive on seasonal return when winning very easily over 2m1f at Downpatrick. Has taken a hike in the ratings but should come on for that run and is a leading contender.

Jerrari was unplaced in his first 7 starts but has looked much improved in his last 2 races. He was runner-up at Kilbeggan in June and then went one better when winning a 15-runner handicap at Roscommon by 3.75 lengths. He is up 8 lbs, but with more improvement likely, he looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

Clonbury Bridge won this in 2021 and was 2nd last year, both times off a 1lb higher mark. Has been chasing on the last 5 starts, completing three of them, winning one, and running well in the other two. UR over the bank course at Punchestown last time and returned here with ground as he likes. He is capable of making the frame at least.

After 22 races without a win, I'm opting for an each-way wager at odds of 18/1. If he can match his 2nd place finish in the handicap chase at Downpatrick from 14 days ago, that should be enough. Still, I believe he might surprise, transitioning from chase to hurdles and take all.

This looks very competitive, and a chance is taken on outsider Half A Chance (hopefully he will live up to his name). He has run better than his final placings suggest on his last two runs and looks well handicapped at present. This drying ground should aid his chances.

Risky one admittedly. But looks very well in off this type of mark, with the jockey taking off a further 7lbs with her claim. He's only registered the 1 career win to date. To be fair, it was an ultra-competitive maiden hurdle, beating Almuhit by 5L. He was going away at the line also. Could have won by further if need be. He had a few decent performers beaten off behind him. I liked his run at this track last season. He finished a decent 5th in a better race than this off a 7lbs higher mark, beaten just over 5L by the winner. Those who finished in front of him are rated higher than this fella. He comes into this fit from a summer campaign on the flat. He ran well on his penultimate run, beaten just 3L back in 3rd place. He's got a big weight here. Jockey helps out with her claim though. If he repeats that course run, he could well outrun his odds here.
Plenty in hand when winning last time and gets whacked up 9lb, with connections putting up a claimer who takes off 7lb. So, has a strong chance of following up here.

A consistent 3 year old Irish filly, she has finished in the first two 4 times from 6 starts in Rules Races, and looks a good prospect to win today with regular jockey Luke McAteer booked to ride. Well drawn in stall 1 with 7 furlongs a suitable distance. First race on yielding ground will hopefully be manageable.

Joseph O'Brien (SR 30%) trained Honeysuckle Rose has only had four runs and has run pretty well at a decent level of form. Winner on second start over seven furlongs on all weather. Decent start to handicap company when third of 12 last time out. This daughter of Bated Breath can go well again for in form connections. Dylan Browne McMonagle (SR 29%) rides.

The model I run suggests Mother Mara can win this one. Mother Mara is currently a reserve horse, but in the larger 15-horse field, it's very possible a couple drop out. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. The model result has been driven by Mother Mara having the second highest RPR of the 15-runner field and a very low weight to carry over this 7f dash.

Last of 7 in the handicap at Leopardstown 18 days ago. However, he will pose a threat to everyone if he can replicate the form he showed when finishing 2nd at Naas in March. Trainer Stephen Thorne boasts an impressive 21% win rate, and Jack Kearney will be riding again with his 3lb claim. With odds of 16/1, I believe an each-way bet is the value here.

Lines have to be drawn and a few excuses made to make a case for Mrs John Harrington's 3 year old Filly FIONA MACCOUL, This Daughter of COULSTY wouldn't have loved the 10f she experienced last time out at Gowran Park, the return back to 7f Certainly looks a positive and if we take her win at Naas In October where she beat the likes of COPACABANA SANDS & SIGH NO MORE who have gone on to win in big contests since then surely this Filly can't be dismissed so easily running off a lowly mark of 73. Top pilot Shane Foley gets the leg up & certainly knows his way round here with a 35.34% place strike rate the past 5 years. Harrington has a 33.77% place strike rate over the sake period with a 32.81% place strike rate with her 2nd time out Handicappers. 25/1 is too big a price for me to ignore.

After showing nothing in 4 maidens, Bear Creek has found rapid improvement since stepping up in trip in handicaps. He was 3rd in a blanket finish at Limerick over 1m4f last month and then won comfortably by 2 lengths over 1m5f at Down Royal 10 days ago. He is 10lbs higher here, but this is only his 7th start, and with more improvement likely, he can follow up.
Much improved and in top form, winning 3-year-old handicaps the last two times. Gave 15 pounds to the second that day, who had won its last race. Up 13 pounds but still looks to be on a winning mark.

The model I run suggests Desmond Castle can win this one. Desmond Castle lines up here with the highest RPR of this 11-runner field but is not penalized for it in the weights. Stpe is carrying the third lowest initial amount of weight and tries the cheekpieces for the first time to aid concentration. 3rd when last out 16 days ago and looks to build on that form here. Moel has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Dam won over 1m4f so stepping up in trip seemed to suit this one last time as was a staying on second in the apprentice Derby at the Curragh. Doesn't look stable first string but the fact young claimer has been onboard both times this one has won including at Leopardstown over 10f in May is noted. Again shaped there as if step up in trip would suit and as holds a Group 3 entry could be on a fair enough mark here.
Has a nice racing weight today. Top amateur jockey booking today on ground and a trip to suit. Nice chance in this field.

The model I run suggests Maskarvel can win this one. Maskarvel lines up here with the second highest RPR of the larger 20-horse field. Maskarvel has shown decent form coming into this with prior second and 4th place finishes in similar company. Alan O'Sullivan on board relieves a further 7 lbs weight and can make the difference over a 2m trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Ostensibly the second string for trainer Gordon Elliott but this No Risk At All gelding cost 100,000 euros as a two year old. Josh Williamson (SR 33%) rides. Actually led by a long way early in last Point start. Not ruled out of a big run here.

This gelding's dam is an unraced half-sister to the impressive hurdle winner and top chaser Journey With Me, as well as the capable hurdler/chaser Yorkist. The Slattery yard is in good shape, and the 7lb claim from the jockey will provide significant assistance here. At 125/1 odds, a modest each-way bet might result in a considerable profit.
